root.markdown:
# PureGamma AI

> **Research intelligence for disciplined decision-making — with clear operating boundaries.**

PureGamma AI turns market context, portfolio-aware research, and repeatable playbooks into a daily decision workflow. It is designed for investors and research teams who want a single, explainable place to review market developments, portfolio context, option research, and paper-trading strategy outputs.

## What this documentation covers

- **Product Guide** — onboarding and the user-facing workflows available today.
- **Platform & Architecture** — how the application, workers, data providers, delivery channels, and paper runtime fit together.
- **Trust & Operations** — security controls, data boundaries, service status, billing, and limitations.
- **Developer Reference** — service boundaries, deployment, and integration contracts for technical teams.

## Product position

PureGamma is a research, analytics, and workflow product. It does **not** place live orders, custody assets, move funds, request wallet signatures, or hold private keys or seed phrases. Trading-related capabilities are limited to research, backtesting, and PAPER/SHADOW runtime modes. Nothing in the product or documentation is investment advice, an offer, or a guarantee of performance.

## Version 1.2

This release reframes the documentation for production use: it separates confirmed functionality from planned integrations, documents delivery and relay boundaries, and provides a technical view alongside the product guide.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  User[Web & iOS users] --> Web[Next.js web application]
  Web --> API[FastAPI application]
  API --> DB[(PostgreSQL / application database)]
  API --> Workers[Background workers & scheduler]
  Workers --> Data[Market, portfolio & model providers]
  Workers --> Reports[Research reports, signals & playbooks]
  Reports --> Notify[Email, Telegram, Slack, iMessage]
  Notify --> Relay[Optional self-hosted Mac relay]
  API --> Runtime[Isolated Nautilus-compatible paper runtime]
```

Start with [Getting started](./product-guide/getting-started.md), then consult the platform and trust sections before connecting an account or enabling a delivery channel.

# Product Guide

Use this section to configure PureGamma, understand the available workflows, and make informed use of the product. Features are governed by your plan, account permissions, connected providers, and the availability of third-party services.

PureGamma is deliberately opinionated about safety: research is separate from execution, account connections are read-only, and delivery preferences are explicit.

Read the pages below in order if you are new to the platform.

# Platform & Architecture

This section is for teams that need a clear operating model before deploying, integrating, or assessing PureGamma. It documents the application boundaries that are implemented today and distinguishes operational contracts from future roadmap work.

The platform is composed of a web and mobile experience, a FastAPI service layer, background workers, provider adapters, durable records, and an isolated research/paper runtime. No component is a live order-routing system.

Production documentation must make boundaries visible. This section describes what data is processed, how access is constrained, which controls are relied upon, and what users should expect when a third-party provider or delivery channel is unavailable.

It is written for customers, administrators, security reviewers, and implementation partners.

# Developer Reference

This reference is for developers and platform operators working with the PureGamma repository or a controlled deployment. It complements the product guide with concrete service boundaries and deployment expectations.

Public product behavior is the authority for customers; implementation details here explain how that behavior is delivered and operated.

children.title: Getting started
children.markdown:
# Getting started

## 1. Create and secure your account

Sign in with the enabled identity provider, review your profile, and choose your preferred language. Use a unique password where password login is available; do not share account access or provider credentials.

## 2. Set your research context

Configure market interests, assets, strategy preferences, and delivery windows. These preferences are used to personalize reports; they do not authorize trading.

## 3. Review the daily workflow

Open the dashboard to review the daily brief, market intelligence, signals, and available playbooks. Research outputs include evidence, source context where available, and confidence-oriented framing. Treat them as decision support, not instructions.

## 4. Connect only what you need

Portfolio and broker connections are optional and read-only. Connectors are subject to provider availability and may require a separate authorization flow. Never provide withdrawal permissions, private keys, seed phrases, or trading credentials.

## 5. Enable delivery deliberately

Email, Telegram, Slack, and the optional iMessage relay are separate delivery paths. Check plan eligibility and verify the destination before enabling a channel. If delivery fails, the report remains available in the product and the event is recorded for retry or support review.

children.title: Core workflows
children.markdown:
# Core workflows

## Daily research loop

1. Shared market intelligence is collected and normalized.
2. The research layer builds a user-aware brief using preferences and, where enabled, portfolio context.
3. You review reports, signals, option research, and playbooks in the product.
4. Eligible delivery channels receive a concise notification or brief.

The separation between shared intelligence and personalized output reduces repeated processing while preserving user-specific context.

## Agent research

The agent experience supports structured research conversations and reports. It uses provider-backed or configured model services, with controls for metering and entitlements. It is not a broker, execution agent, or financial adviser.

## Signals and playbooks

Signals communicate a research hypothesis, confidence framing, and relevant context. Playbooks make the intended research process repeatable. Their availability and parameters can vary by plan and runtime status.

## Backtesting and paper runtime

Backtests are research tools with documented assumptions. Paper and shadow modes simulate strategy lifecycle and projections without sending live market orders. Historical or simulated performance is not indicative of future results.

children.title: Portfolio & read-only connections
children.markdown:
# Portfolio & read-only connections

PureGamma can present portfolio context only through explicitly connected, read-only sources. The product is designed so that connected credentials are processed server-side and are not returned to the browser, iOS client, or language model.

## Supported connection model

- **Plaid Investments**: intended for holdings, securities, and investment transactions; never for trading or money movement.
- **Interactive Brokers (IBKR)**: OAuth-based portfolio access where configured and supported.
- **Exchange keys**: read-only integrations must not have trading, transfer, or withdrawal permissions.
- **On-chain wallets**: public-address data only; the product does not ask for wallet signing or private keys.

## Data freshness

Provider data can be delayed, incomplete, or pending. The product should surface freshness and connector status rather than imply real-time completeness. A successful connection does not make every historical record immediately available.

## Disconnecting

You may remove a connection from the product. If a provider authorization must also be revoked, complete the revocation in that provider’s account portal. Review the Privacy & Data Handling page for the persistence and deletion model.

children.title: Research, options & backtests
children.markdown:
# Research, options & backtests

## Market and company research

PureGamma combines configured public and licensed sources with structured research prompts and analyst-style reports. Availability depends on the deployment’s provider configuration and source health. Missing or degraded sources should produce a transparent status rather than fabricated precision.

## Options research

The options experience uses public Deribit market data for supported BTC and ETH option research. It can organize IV, Greeks, liquidity, and theta-cost context for long-gamma screening. It does not trade derivatives, place orders, or manage collateral.

## Backtest discipline

Backtests must state their assumptions, including market data, fees, fills, slippage, and look-ahead controls. A backtest is an analytical scenario, not a promise of execution quality or returns.

## Strategy catalog

Strategy entries document the hypothesis, market regime, risk controls, and validation status. A strategy may be visible while still unavailable for paper runtime; status in the product is the source of truth.

children.title: Notifications & delivery
children.markdown:
# Notifications & delivery

PureGamma separates content generation from delivery. A report may be successfully generated even if a third-party notification provider is unavailable. Delivery attempts are recorded so failures can be retried without producing duplicate messages.

## Available channels

- In-product reports and dashboard
- Email, where SMTP is configured
- Telegram and Slack, where configured
- Optional self-hosted iMessage delivery through a verified Mac relay

## Delivery controls

Channel availability depends on your plan, verified destination, user preferences, and provider configuration. Daily iMessage delivery is an entitlement-controlled feature for eligible plans.

Each delivery is designed around an idempotency key, which prevents an automatic retry from intentionally sending the same message twice. If you need to change a recipient, verify the new destination before re-enabling delivery.

See [Relay communication](../../platform-and-architecture/relay-communication.md) for the security model used by the iMessage path.

children.title: System architecture
children.markdown:
# System architecture

## Runtime components

| Layer | Responsibility | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Web and iOS clients | User interaction, localization, account workflows | No long-lived provider secrets |
| FastAPI application | Authentication, APIs, entitlements, orchestration | Validates identity and business rules |
| Database | Users, reports, delivery records, subscriptions, projections | Tenant-scoped application data |
| Workers and scheduler | Reports, synchronization, notification jobs | Idempotent, retry-aware execution |
| Provider adapters | Data, models, billing, notifications | Isolated integrations and fallback handling |
| Nautilus-compatible runtime | Backtests and PAPER/SHADOW strategy execution | Separate service; live trading disabled |

## Data flow

Requests flow from the client to the API, which authorizes the user and coordinates durable work. Background workers perform scheduled or queued jobs, store results, and invoke notification adapters. Provider failures are handled as explicit degraded states.

## Design principles

- Separate user experience from secrets and provider adapters.
- Keep shared intelligence distinct from personalized reports.
- Use durable ledgers and idempotency at billing, delivery, and runtime-projection boundaries.
- Isolate paper runtime control from the primary web request path.
- Keep live trading unavailable by design, configuration, and safety tests.

children.title: Relay communication
children.markdown:
# Relay communication

## Why a relay exists

Apple does not provide a general server-side iMessage API. PureGamma therefore offers an optional, self-hosted macOS relay for users or deployments that choose iMessage delivery. The relay is not a cloud bypass and does not read the private Messages database.

## Message path

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant PG as PureGamma API
  participant R as Customer-managed Mac relay
  participant A as Apple Messages
  participant U as Verified recipient
  PG->>R: Signed HTTPS request + idempotency key
  R->>R: Validate timestamp and HMAC-SHA256
  R->>R: Persist delivery state
  R->>A: AppleScript sends message or media
  A-->>U: iMessage delivery
  R-->>PG: Delivery result
```

## Security contract

The API signs the raw request body using HMAC-SHA256 over `{timestamp}.{raw_body}`. The relay verifies the timestamp and signature before it accepts a delivery. An idempotency key lets the relay safely return the result of a prior attempt rather than duplicate a message.

The relay must be network-restricted, hold its shared secret outside source control, and run on a Mac signed into an account authorized to use Messages. The relay uses AppleScript to send; it does not access the Messages database. Voice media is converted on the relay to the expected iMessage voice-bubble format when applicable.

If the relay is offline, delivery fails transparently and the report remains in-product.

children.title: Research runtime & trading safety
children.markdown:
# Research runtime & trading safety

PureGamma uses an isolated Nautilus-compatible service for research, backtests, and PAPER/SHADOW strategy execution. This service is controlled through an internal runtime client and projects relevant state back to the primary application database.

## Supported operating modes

- **Research**: analysis and backtesting.
- **Paper**: simulated positions, fills, and portfolio projections.
- **Shadow**: evaluates strategy behavior without live orders.

## Explicitly excluded

- Live order placement
- Asset custody, transfers, or withdrawals
- Wallet signing, private-key handling, or seed-phrase collection
- Broker execution routing

## Safety controls

Runtime commands are permission-checked, state-aware, and recorded through durable projections. Restart recovery and idempotent projection protect the primary database from duplicate runtime events. A deployment should expose runtime status honestly: native Nautilus support is used where available; otherwise a clearly labeled mock bridge may be used for non-production or supported fallback scenarios.

Research quality controls include validation documentation, no-look-ahead checks, risk scoring, and stated backtest assumptions. These controls reduce operational ambiguity; they do not eliminate market risk.

children.title: Data & model pipeline
children.markdown:
# Data & model pipeline

## Inputs

The platform’s data layer is adapter-based. It can use market-data sources, public research sources, portfolio providers, public on-chain data, and model providers configured for the deployment. Providers should be identified in the product’s data-source status surface.

## Processing

Shared market intelligence is generated once per run where possible. Personalized reports are then built with a user’s permitted preferences and portfolio context. This is a performance and privacy boundary: the system should not turn one user’s private context into shared market content.

## Model-provider boundary

Language-model access is behind a provider abstraction with metering and entitlement controls. Provider keys remain in the server-controlled environment. Model output is constrained by product prompts and evidence policies, but it may still be incomplete or incorrect; users must verify material claims.

## Quality and resilience

Jobs are scheduled, retry-aware, and observable. A source outage, stale feed, or model-provider error must yield a clear degraded state, not an invented data point. Where fallback data is present in development interfaces, it must be labeled and must not be represented as live production data.

children.title: Security, privacy & compliance
children.markdown:
# Security, privacy & compliance

## Core security posture

PureGamma uses authenticated API boundaries, server-side provider credentials, tenant-aware data access, signed integration requests, and operational logging. The browser and iOS client do not receive Stripe, model, broker, exchange, Plaid, or relay secrets.

## Sensitive connection data

Read-only connector tokens and API materials belong in server-controlled configuration and must be encrypted before durable storage where the connector is implemented. Users must never supply private keys, seed phrases, withdrawal permissions, or trading-enabled exchange keys.

## Payment and webhook integrity

Stripe webhooks are signature-validated and deduplicated by event identifier. Billing writes are designed to be idempotent and unknown plan mappings are routed for manual review rather than silently granting access.

## Data and product boundaries

Portfolio connections are analytical only. Research, reports, and signals are informational. Live trading is disabled. The product is not a broker-dealer, investment adviser, exchange, custodian, or wallet provider.

## Responsible use

Do not treat product output as personalized investment advice. Review sources, validate assumptions, consider your own risk tolerance, and consult qualified advisers where appropriate. Privacy and legal terms governing your deployment remain controlling.

children.title: Billing, credits & entitlements
children.markdown:
# Billing, credits & entitlements

Plans determine access to capabilities such as agent usage, report volume, delivery channels, and administrative features. Credits are metered product units; they are not currency, an investment, or a stored-value account.

## Billing workflow

Stripe Checkout Sessions, Payment Links, subscriptions, the customer portal, and signed webhooks support the billing flow where Stripe is enabled. The application maintains local subscription and entitlement state so access decisions remain auditable.

## Credit controls

Usage is recorded through a credit ledger and metering services. Entitlements are checked before a protected action is performed. Daily delivery and agent activity can be subject to plan limits, budgets, and operational controls.

## Reconciliation and exceptions

Webhook handling is idempotent. If a payment link or price cannot be mapped to a known plan, the event is held for manual review rather than automatically changing a user’s privileges. If billing status appears incorrect, contact support with the account email and the relevant invoice or checkout reference; do not send payment credentials.

Pricing, plan availability, taxes, and refund terms are governed by the terms displayed at purchase and may vary by market.

children.title: Service status, limitations & roadmap
children.markdown:
# Service status, limitations & roadmap

## Implemented product foundations

The repository includes FastAPI and Next.js applications, account flows, reports, signals, playbooks, Stripe billing, credits and entitlements, configurable model providers, notifications, a self-hosted iMessage relay, scheduled workers, mock/native backtest selection, strategy control, and PAPER/SHADOW runtime support.

## Important availability boundaries

Some interfaces are intentionally designed ahead of a fully enabled provider integration. Depending on the deployment, portfolio connections, data-source pages, daily push controls, or runtime surfaces can show clearly labeled fallback data until the backed service is configured. Plaid and other connectors remain subject to provider configuration, approval, and data availability.

## Roadmap discipline

A documented contract, prototype, or UI surface is not a production commitment. Planned work may include broader provider connectivity, expanded portfolio NAV synchronization, enterprise data imports, and additional runtime integrations. Product availability is confirmed only by the in-product status and applicable agreement.

## Reporting an issue

For a delivery, data, or billing incident, record the time, channel, expected outcome, and any visible error. Do not include secrets, private keys, full access tokens, or payment-card details in a support request.

children.title: API & service boundaries
children.markdown:
# API & service boundaries

The API layer is a FastAPI application organized around routers and services for authentication, agents, market research, reports, signals, playbooks, portfolio context, billing, options, notifications, and runtime control.

## Boundary map

| Area | Service responsibility | External boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Auth | Session and identity workflows | Google / Apple where enabled |
| Research | Reports, agent runs, signals, playbooks | Model and data providers |
| Portfolio | Read-only connection and synchronization contracts | Plaid, IBKR, exchanges, public wallets |
| Billing | Checkout, subscriptions, credits, entitlements | Stripe |
| Notifications | Preferences, delivery records, channel dispatch | Email, Slack, Telegram, Mac relay |
| Runtime | Strategy lifecycle and paper-state synchronization | Nautilus-compatible service |

## Extension rules

Add providers behind a dedicated adapter or service. Validate external payloads, keep secrets server-side, classify errors as retryable or terminal, and record stable identifiers for idempotency. New product endpoints should enforce identity, tenant isolation, entitlements, and an explicit operational status.

Do not introduce live execution paths without a separate, reviewed product and compliance decision.

children.title: Deployment & operations
children.markdown:
# Deployment & operations

## Services

A controlled deployment consists of the API, web application, database, background workers/scheduler, optional isolated runtime, and optional Mac relay. Docker Compose configuration is provided for local and production-oriented environments. The relay is a distinct macOS service and cannot be hosted as a Linux-only replacement for Apple Messages.

## Configuration

Secrets and provider credentials are environment-managed. Configuration covers identity, database, Stripe, model providers, notification channels, portfolio connectors, public data sources, runtime control, and relay signing. Production validation should reject insecure defaults such as mock delivery where a real provider is required.

## Observability

Operators should monitor API health, worker queues, scheduled jobs, data-source freshness, delivery outcomes, webhook processing, subscription reconciliation, and runtime availability. Use correlation identifiers and idempotency keys when investigating retries.

## Release checklist

Before enabling a production feature: validate secrets, restrict network access, confirm webhook signatures, run security and integration tests, verify delivery destinations, document provider limitations, and confirm that the UI does not present fallback data as live. Keep deployment and rollback procedures in the operations runbook.
